We need retrosynthesis route for target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We need up to 3 steps, leaves commercially available, total price <=9999 (we can't check price but assume typical). Need to propose route using templates.

We need to find disconnections: The molecule has a sulfonamide linking two aromatic rings, and an amide attached to a phenyl via a trans-alkene (styryl amide). So possible retrosynthesis: break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonic acid) and an aniline. Also break amide to give an acid chloride and aniline.

Potential steps:
1. Disconnection of sulfonamide: target -> sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2Cl) + aniline (Ar-NH2). Template likely exists: sulfonamide formation from sulfonyl chloride and amine. Use template ID maybe from search earlier? We saw template with sulfonamide formation from sulfonyl chloride and amine (reaction_id 723274). That template retro_smarts: [#7:4]-[S(=O)(=O)-c]>>Cl-C(=O)-Ar + [#7:4]-[SH](=O)=O (maybe). Actually that template seems to form sulfonamide from sulfonyl chloride and thiol? Not sure.

But we can still propose using known chemistry: sulfonyl chloride + aniline.

Second disconnection: amide formation from acid chloride and aniline (or from carboxylic acid + amine via coupling). The amide is attached to trans-alkene chain: C=C-C(=O)-NH-Ph-NH2? Actually structure: /C=C/C(=O)N c3ccccc3N . So amide carbonyl attached to an aniline (para-aminophenyl) and the alkene attached to aromatic sulfonyl phenyl.

So we can break amide to give acid chloride (or acid) and aniline (para-aminophenyl). The alkene part is a cinnamoyl moiety: trans-CH=CH-CO- . Could be formed via Heck coupling of aryl bromide with acrylate then convert to amide? Or via Wittig? Simpler: use commercially available trans-cinnamic acid (C=CC(=O)O) then convert to acid chloride then amidate with aniline. Cinnamic acid is cheap.

Thus propose route:
Step 1: Form sulfonamide: React 4-methyl aniline (p-toluidine) with 4-(chlorosulfonyl)phenyl (or 4-(sulfonyl chloride) phenyl) that also bears the cinnamoyl group? Wait the sulfonyl phenyl also attached to the cinnamoyl chain via para position? Actually target: sulfonyl phenyl (c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2) attached to sulfonamide linking to tolyl ring. So sulfonyl phenyl has the cinnamoyl amide substituent at para position relative to sulfonyl group.

Thus we can first construct the sulfonyl phenyl with the cinnamoyl amide substituent, then attach sulfonamide to tolyl.

So retrosynthesis:
Target -> (1) sulfonyl chloride intermediate: 4-(cinnamoylamido)phenylsulfonyl chloride + p-toluidine (4-methylaniline). Then sulfonamide formation gives target.

Now need to get 4-(cinnamoylamido)phenylsulfonyl chloride. This can be made from 4-(cinnamoylamido)benzenesulfonic acid (or sulfonic acid) then chlorination, or from 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride via Suzuki coupling? Simpler: start from 4-aminophenyl sulfonyl chloride (p-aminobenzenesulfonyl chloride) then amidate? But sulfonyl chloride reacts with amine to give sulfonamide, not amide. So need to attach amide to aromatic ring before sulfonyl chloride formation.

Thus alternative: start from 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride, do Suzuki coupling with trans-cinnamoyl aniline? Not straightforward.

Maybe better route: first form amide on phenyl ring (para to sulfonyl group) via acylation of aniline (para-aminophenyl) with trans-cinnamoyl chloride (from trans-cinnamic acid). That gives 4-(cinnamoylamino)aniline (p-aminophenyl cinnamamide). Then sulfonylate that aniline's other position? Actually we need sulfonyl group attached to that ring, not amine. The sulfonyl group is attached to the ring via S(=O)2 linking to the tolyl amine. So the sulfonyl phenyl is the one bearing the amide substituent; the sulfonyl group is attached to the ring via S(=O)2 to the tolyl amine. So the sulfonyl phenyl does not have an amine; the amide is attached to that phenyl via a carbonyl attached to an aniline (c3ccccc3N). Wait the amide is C(=O)N-Ph-NH2, meaning the carbonyl attached to an aniline (anilide) which has an NH2 para? Actually "Nc3ccccc3N" indicates the amide nitrogen attached to phenyl which also has an NH2 at para? The SMILES: ...C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N . That is an anilide where the aniline has an amino group at para? The phenyl is "c3ccccc3N" meaning an aniline (aniline with NH2 attached to ring). So the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl that also has an NH2 substituent (maybe ortho?). So the amide is attached to an aniline that also has an NH2 group (anilide with free amine). So the product has a free aniline on that phenyl.

Thus the target contains two aniline groups: one on tolyl (connected via sulfonamide) and one on the phenyl attached to amide (free NH2). So we need to preserve that.

Thus retrosynthesis: break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride attached to phenyl with amide substituent, and p-toluidine.

Break amide to give trans-cinnamic acid (or acid chloride) and the aniline (c3ccccc3N). So the phenyl with free NH2 is the amine component.

Thus steps:
Step A (final): sulfonamide formation between p-toluidine and sulfonyl chloride (aryl sulfonyl chloride) that already contains the amide substituent.

Step B: synthesis of that aryl sulfonyl chloride: start from 4-(cinnamoylamido)benzenesulfonic acid (or sulfonyl chloride) via chlorination of sulfonic acid. Could obtain 4-(cinnamoylamido)benzenesulfonyl chloride directly from 4-(cinnamoylamido)benzenesulfonic acid (commercial?). Might be easier: start from 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride, do Buchwald-Hartwig amination with aniline? Not.

Alternative: start from 4-aminobenzenesulfonyl chloride, protect the amine, then acylate with cinnamic acid, then deprotect. But we need the amide attached to the ring, not the sulfonyl group.

Actually the amide is attached to the phenyl via carbonyl to an aniline (the phenyl with NH2). So the phenyl bearing the amide is the same phenyl that also has the sulfonyl group? No, the sulfonyl phenyl is the one attached to sulfonamide; the amide phenyl is separate (c3ccccc3N). So the sulfonyl phenyl does NOT have the amide; the amide is attached to the sulfonyl phenyl via the alkene chain: /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2 attached to the sulfonyl phenyl at para position. So the sulfonyl phenyl has a substituent: a trans-alkenyl amide attached to an aniline.

Thus the sulfonyl phenyl is substituted at para with a styryl amide (C=C-CO-NH-Ph-NH2). So we need to construct that substituent on the sulfonyl phenyl before sulfonyl chloride formation.

Thus route:
1. Start from 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride (commercial). Perform Suzuki coupling with trans-alkenyl boronic acid that carries the amide? Could use trans-3-(4-aminophenyl)acrylamide boronic acid? Might be complex.

Simplify: Build the aryl-alkenyl amide via Heck coupling of 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride with trans-cinnamyl amide (like N-phenylacrylamide). Actually trans-cinnamoyl aniline (C=CC(=O)Nc3ccccc3N) is an acrylamide. Could be prepared by reacting trans-cinnamic acid chloride with p-aminophenyl (aniline). Then we need to attach that to the sulfonyl phenyl via a C-C double bond (Heck) at para position. So we need a bromophenyl sulfonyl chloride and do Heck with the acrylamide.

Thus steps:
Step 1: Prepare trans-cinnamoyl aniline (C=CC(=O)Nc3ccccc3N) from trans-cinnamic acid (commercial) via conversion to acid chloride (SOCl2) then amidation with p-phenylenediamine? Actually need aniline with NH2 on ring; the amide nitrogen attaches to the phenyl, not the other way. So we need N-(4-aminophenyl)acrylamide. That can be made by reacting trans-cinnamic acid chloride with 4-aminophenylamine (p-phenylenediamine) giving the amide with free NH2 on the phenyl.

Step 2: Perform Heck coupling between 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride and the acrylamide (trans) to give the aryl-alkenyl amide attached to sulfonyl chloride.

Step 3: Sulfonamide formation with p-toluidine to give final product.

All leaves: 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride (commercial), trans-cinnamic acid (commercial), p-phenylenediamine (commercial), p-toluidine (commercial), SOCl2 (reagent). All likely cheap.

We need to provide JSON route with reactions and template IDs. We need template IDs for Heck coupling (C-C double bond formation) and sulfonamide formation, and amide formation (acyl chloride + amine). We can search for templates.

Search for amide formation: functional_groups_broken: acyl chloride, formed: amide.
